Level 2 · Build

Level 2: Agentic Application Security Professional

Move from knowing security concepts to engineering secure agentic applications.

Open the live courseSee pathways

Eight core lessons live; verification and pipeline modules planned

Who it is for
Software and platform engineers, application security engineers and AI/ML engineers who ship agents.
Before you start
Level 1 or the entry diagnostic. Working knowledge of one programming language and HTTP APIs.
Capstone evidence
A secure-agent application project with abuse cases, a verification report and a code and configuration review.
How it is assessed
Observed build-and-verify task, negative tests that must fail closed, and a written review defended to an assessor.

Modules and evidence

Each module ends in an artefact that goes into your portfolio.

ModuleYou will be able toEvidence
Prompt and context securityExplain the limits of instruction hierarchy; separate trusted and untrusted context; track provenance and enforce policy.Prompt-injection test corpus, context design and regression results
Tool, API and MCP securityScope capabilities; validate inputs and encode outputs; verify server identity, discovery, revocation and provenance.Secure tool gateway, tool manifest review and abuse-case tests
Agent identity and delegationUse workload identity, short-lived credentials, audience restriction, privilege ceilings and revocation.Identity and delegation model with negative authorisation tests
Memory, RAG and data securityEnforce tenant isolation and retrieval filtering; handle provenance, poisoning, retention and deletion.RAG threat model, poisoned-source test and data-access evidence
Code execution and isolationSandbox ephemeral workloads; restrict filesystem, network and egress; isolate secrets; limit resources.Isolated execution environment and escape-resistance test plan
Model and AI supply chainRecord model provenance and artefacts; scan and sign; gate deployment; plan rollback.Model and software bill of materials with provenance record
Secure implementation and verificationWrite security requirements; review code; run SAST, DAST and API tests; build release gates.AISVS-informed verification report and CI security gates

Planned lessons

These lessons are not written yet. They close gaps found in the audit.

  • P1Model pipelines: data, training, registry and signing Planned
    Closes the GAIPS development-pipelines and MLOps cluster: data lineage, training and fine-tuning pipelines, CI/CD, model registry, artefact signing, evaluation gates and rollback.
  • P2Fine-tuning, adapters and alignment: poisoning, backdoors and limits Planned
    Closes the model customisation and alignment cluster: dataset lineage, backdoor and poisoning risk, safety regression, and why alignment is not a security boundary.
  • P4Privacy, sensitive data and logging in agent systems Planned
    Prompt and log retention, leakage, minimisation, deletion, training reuse, residency and access control as data moves between tools, providers, logs and retrieval stores.
